method: Extraction yield is the share of the dry coffee that dissolved into the cup. Dissolved solids = TDS% / 100 × beverage mass, and extraction yield = dissolved solids / dose × 100, so 18 g of coffee brewing 36 g of espresso at 9% TDS gives 3.24 g of solids and an 18% yield. Results are rounded to three decimals before the 18-22% extraction band and the TDS strength band are assigned, so a reading of exactly 22% stays inside the window. Brew ratio and water retained are shown only when the brew water is supplied; beverage mass may not exceed water plus dose. TDS must be measured with a refractometer on a cooled, stirred sample - the page only does the arithmetic. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
